articles.title: An Inside Look at the Relay Market Powering Token Resellers and Fraud
articles.summary:
An Inside Look at the Relay Market Powering Token Resellers and Fraud

Fascinating investigation by Matt Lenhard into the market that has grown up around reselling LLM tokens at a discount by pooling API keys from various sources.

This looks to be mostly a thing in China. Resellers sell access to an LLM proxy that offers significant discounts on regular API pricing, which they achieve by abusing free trials, proxying through unprotected support bots, or sometimes through stolen credit cards or chargeback attacks.

The software they are using for these proxies is open source - mostly one-api and its more actively developed fork new-api, both legitimate API proxy products which can be used to load. balance requests across a pool of API credentials.

The buyers are seeking cheap tokens, avoiding geo-restrictions, and in some cases collecting data for model distillation.

I've been cautious about exposing my own LLM-driven applications publicly out of fear of abuse leading to big token bills. The existence of this marketplace makes me even more cautious: there's now an entire ecosystem that can profit from finding a new unprotected endpoint to exploit.

LLM vendors really need to get better at offering strict caps for their API keys. I want my LLM apps to stop working the moment they hit a dollar threshold I've set for a period of time.

Here's the (Chinese language) forum thread that served as the principal source for Matt's article.

Via Hacker News

Tags: ai, generative-ai, llms, llm-pricing, ai-ethics, ai-in-china

articles.title: Furious review – a proper grownup thriller that’s powered by sheer female rage
articles.summary:
This crime drama about a female serial killer is enormously entertaining TV that demands you pay attention

Furious is well named. It is powered throughout its eight-episode run by an unfaltering current of female rage. It is the creation of Elizabeth Meriwether, who gave us last year’s astonishing Dying for Sex (starring Michelle Williams as a woman with terminal cancer discovering the range and depth of her sexuality for the first time) and 2022’s brisk, brilliant The Dropout (the tale of Elizabeth Holmes, the disgraced founder of blood-testing company, Theranos). They were both based on true stories. Furious was apparently inspired by the 1987 film Black Widow, starring Theresa Russell and Debra Winger, but it has jettisoned the marry-and-murder-for-money plot and contemporised the rest so thoroughly that the result hardly seems to merit the dutiful hat-tip the publicity has given it.

Meriwether is the writer of the first three episodes, the rest are divided among four women and one man. The drama itself is dominated by three complicated and fascinating female characters, played by Emmy Rossum, Lola Petticrew (who gave an extraordinary performance in 2024’s Say Nothing) and Quincy Tyler Bernstine. A fantastic supporting cast and a dense, lean, evocative script make this television for grownups, television to pay attention to and to entertain you enormously.

Furious is on Disney+
